subject: Repricing and rollback plan for NovaEdge migration
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@novaedge.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.procure@novaedge.com>, Elan Kaur <elan@cloudprime.io>
Date: 2027-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pricing and fallback / rollback questions for migration

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Procurement and infra are aligned on the technical fit but we need clarity on economics and rollback safeguards before we present to finance. A few asks from our side: 

1) Can you confirm an apples-to-apples monthly figure if we move from our current provider (CloudPrime) to Redwood for inference — we need both sustained-rate and burst pricing (concurrent slots vs consumption).
2) We want a clear migration credit: a single recovery credit vs staged pilot credits — which gives us the least execution risk?
3) If performance regressions hit in production (KV cache mismatch on our long-tail chat flows), what’s the documented rollback runbook and SLA/credit formula?

We also have legal questions on data retention and audit log export that Elan will follow up on, but pricing + rollback is the gating blocker.

Can you put together an updated commercial with explicit rollback milestones and the term-sheet we can share with finance by EOD Friday?

— Sanjay
Director, Platform Engineering
NovaEdge
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@novaedge.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.procure@novaedge.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-30T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing and fallback / rollback questions for migration

Hi Sanjay — thanks, good questions. Drafting the commercial now; high level answers below and I will attach a term sheet + runbook.

- Pricing: Two options we recommend: 1) Consumption-first (per-token + embedding units) with a capped burst pool for peak concurrency; 2) Slot-reservation (concurrent slots) for predictable latency at higher committed spend. For NovaEdge’s profile (chat-heavy, long-tail KV cache usage) the consumption+burst option usually lowers unit cost for volume growth while preserving a soft floor for latency.

- Migration credits: We can offer a two-stage credit: up-front pilot credit (covers pilot egress and benchmark runs) + a post-go-live stabilization credit that unlocks after 30 days if latency and accuracy targets are met. The alternative is a single larger up-front recovery credit — which reduces short-term cash outlay for you but gives less signal on production fit. My recommendation: two-stage (pilot + stabilization).

- Rollback/runbook & SLA: We will provide a rollback playbook that lists: canary gating (1% traffic -> 10% -> 50%), KV cache parity checks, automated snapshot/export of session state, and a documented time-to-fallback path to the previous model variant or region. SLA credits scale with minutes of sustained SLO breach over the 30-day stabilization window. I will itemize exact credit calculation in the term sheet.

I’m attaching: novaedge-term-sheet-v3.pdf (commercials + rollback clauses) and migration-runbook-v2.xlsx (technical checkpoints & milestones).

Can you confirm which procurement contact needs the final DocuSign link and whether you prefer the pilot credit to be structured as a usage credit or a one-time invoice credit?

Thanks — will follow up with Laura (ops) and Karthik (solutions) to lock the runbook details.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.procure@novaedge.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T08:17:00-08:00
Subject: internal: approval for two-stage credit & technical rollback wording

Markus / Karthik,

Quick internal note before we finalize term-sheet language for NovaEdge (DEAL-78319):

- Two-stage credit is fine but limit the total exposure to 10% of first 6 months' committed spend. That gives procurement a headline number and caps our risk.
- Add explicit KV cache parity tests in the canary checklist: sample 10k session prefixes and verify identical next-token distribution within an RMS threshold. If we fail parity twice in a row, we trigger automatic rollback and a full diagnostic window (our engineers + NovaEdge).
- Pricing tweak: offer consumption-first with a guaranteed unit-price floor for first 90 days if they hit baseline volume targets — prevents surprises for finance.

I’ll sign off on exact credit numbers once you confirm the procurement preference (usage credit vs invoice credit).

Laura
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@novaedge.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.procure@novaedge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-02T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Final commercial & rollback guardrails (DEAL-78319)

Hi Sanjay / Marta — attaching the finalized term sheet and runbook (same file names). Summary of the changes we agreed internally: 

1) Commercial: consumption-first pricing with a 90-day unit-price floor (applies if baseline monthly tokens >= 200M). Burst pool for concurrency up to 2x baseline included for first 60 days.
2) Credits: two-stage credit structure capped at 10% of the first 6 months' committed spend. Pilot credit applied as usage credit (applies to pilot activity in the pilot project id). Stabilization credit issued as invoice credit after 30-day stabilization if latency and quality gates pass.
3) Rollback runbook: explicit canary gates (1% -> 10% -> 50%), KV cache parity test (10k-prefix RMS threshold), automated session snapshot and export, and a documented fallback to the previous model variant or region within the 2-hour target. SLA credit formula is embedded in Section 4.2 of the term sheet.
4) DocuSign: will send to marta.procure@novaedge.com unless you prefer otherwise.

Next steps: Marta to confirm preference on invoice vs usage credit for the stabilization bucket (we recommended invoice credit), and Elan will coordinate the legal/data questions separately. If acceptable I’ll route the DocuSign and set a kickoff for the pilot benchmarking next Tuesday.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Markus
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: novaedge-term-sheet-v3.pdf (commercials + SLA math), migration-runbook-v2.xlsx (canary checklist & test vectors)
